title: Publish of a view draft takes a draft-version precondition, so an unpinned draft write cannot be published by Save to this view (after #36137)
body:
repo:objectstack#7 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jTeURPvEm465RcoYEC

Follow-up from #36137 (direction B, PR #36318). Found by the dev and the L1 on PR #36318 (L1 7076070176); filed by the seat. Parent: #36137.

## What happens

PR #36318 pins the view settings panel's draft save, so a settings save that crosses "Save to this view" (draft write, then publish) is now refused instead of overwriting the draft. Direction B covers only the writers that are pinned. One writer is not: the draft branch of `ObjectStackAdapter.updateView` (rename, pin to top, set as default on a view that has an unpublished draft) still reads the draft, merges and writes it back with no version precondition. It can land in the same window between the draft write and the publish, and the publish then sends its change out for everyone. Ruling 7058616478 on #35955 says an unpublished draft is never published on someone else's behalf, so the window is still open, only narrower.

## Why the client cannot close it alone

`MetadataClient.publish` takes no precondition on the draft's version. Every new draft writer would have to remember its own pin, and a missed one reopens the window.

## To do (direction A on #36137)

1. Give the `/meta` publish door a draft-version precondition (for example `If-Match` on the draft's version), refused with the ADR-0112 envelope (`409 METADATA_CONFLICT`) when the draft moved.
2. `MetadataClient.publish` accepts and sends it; "Save to this view" passes the version its own draft write returned.
3. Pin `updateView`'s draft branch the same way #36318 pins the settings panel, or route it through the same pinned write.

This changes the publish door and the client, so it is a protocol face: its L2 runs on the rules/schema face at the contract-review tier.

## Acceptance

- A test interleaves an `updateView` draft write between "Save to this view"'s draft write and its publish: the publish is refused and nothing unreviewed is published.
- A test pins the door's refusal code and status.

Blocked-by: #36318 (the pinned settings save must be on `main` first)

## Grade
p2 · area:ux · domain:rest. Same harm as #36137 on a narrower path: a draft someone has not reviewed can be published for everyone.
